enforcement_note: Nothing forces the agent to read this table or to load what it selects; loading happens at prompt time, inside the agent's own reasoning, where no hook runs. tests/test_governance_library.py::ChecklistSelection enforces that the table stays internally consistent -- every category it names has a rule file, every rule is reachable -- which is the part that can be checked. Whether it was consulted cannot.
note: The single table governing which checklists load. Both .ai/03-planning/ and .ai/05-domains/ are selected from here, and both skills read this file rather than restating the logic. It lived in 05-domains/manifest.json until plan-review checklists arrived and a second copy would have been needed -- two tables are two answers to one question.
selection_rule: Load a checklist rule when its workflow_phase matches the phase you are in AND its task_size_required contains the declared task size AND (its tech_stack_required is empty OR intersects the project's stack). Within Phase 2, `contexts` narrows further to what the task actually touches.

task_sizes.typo_fix: Single-line changes, comment or wording edits.
task_sizes.small_change: A function added or logic updated within an existing module.
task_sizes.new_module: A new feature, service, or module.

task_size_is_declared: The agent declares task size at Phase 1, before the work exists. It is deliberately NOT derived from `git diff --stat`: at planning time the diff is empty, and deriving it afterwards would load the checklists after the code they were meant to guide. Being a judgement, it is stated in the plan so the user can object while objecting is still cheap.

1.when: Designing the task, before any code exists. Reviews the plan.
1.note: Phase-1 rules are never gated on tech stack. A plan's problem statement is no better or worse for being written in Go, so a stack filter here would only ever exclude a question that still applied.

2.when: Reviewing work that exists. Reviews the code.
2.note: Phase-2 rules narrow by `contexts` below and by tech stack, because a SQL question genuinely does not apply to a project with no database.

contexts_note: Phase-2 only. Phase 1 has no context map: which questions a plan must answer does not depend on what the plan turns out to touch, and a plan that has not yet decided whether it needs a database still has to say what problem it solves.
